ov: Eared seals with external ear flaps, long front flippers and the ability to walk on all fours. There are six living species, found from subarctic to tropical waters in both hemispheres.

why.dg: Attacks are rare, but it can be very unsafe to get within about 2.5 metres.
why.et: Seals and sea lions are hunted for meat and blubber; California sea lions were once hunted for hides and animal feed.

rg: Coasts from subarctic to tropical waters in both the Northern and Southern hemispheres.
df: Fish such as sardines, and other sea creatures.

cf.tip: A sea lion has visible ear flaps and can walk on all four flippers. The true seals are the earless seals.

fx: Sea lions can reach about 56 km/h in the water.
